evidence.finding: Every interval from 09:15 through 11:45 recalculates to exactly 26.0 percentage points above the reported service level; intervals before 09:15 reconcile correctly.

Using the defined formula, actual service level was below the 80% target only at 09:15 (74.42%) and 09:45 (78.21%); all later intervals recalculate above target despite the dashboard remaining below target.
Across 09:15-11:45, actual offered volume totaled 844 calls versus 841 forecast, effectively on plan overall, although several individual intervals were moderately above forecast.
Logged-in staffing remained constant at 49, productive staffing stayed at 45-46, and adherence remained between 91.84% and 93.88% throughout the window.
Queue results show localized, intermittent delays while other queues retained strong service, inconsistent with the dashboard's uniform and sustained 26-point degradation.
No routing or platform event was recorded to corroborate the abrupt, exact reporting offset beginning at 09:15.

primary_root_cause_detail: Beginning exactly at 09:15, the dashboard service-level value is consistently 26.0 percentage points below the supplied metric definition. For example, 64 / (88 - 2) = 74.4186%, while the dashboard reports 48.4186%. The same fixed discrepancy persists through 11:45, confirming a reporting or calculation defect rather than sustained operational degradation.
recommended_actions: Correct the dashboard calculation or transformation that began subtracting 26 percentage points at 09:15.
Backfill and republish service-level results from 09:15 through 11:45 using the defined formula.
Add automated reconciliation between displayed service level and answered_within_threshold divided by offered_calls minus short_abandoned_calls.
Alert on abrupt fixed-offset metric changes and retain the moderate interval-level volume variances for routine operational review.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: There were moderate interval-level increases, but aggregate incident-window demand was only 0.4% above forecast and cannot explain an exact 26-point reporting offset.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained at 49, exceeding forecast requirements of 36-40 agents, with productive staffing stable at 45-46.
Adherence remained stable above 91.8% and did not decline at incident onset.
AHT remained near or below forecast in most incident intervals and did not increase in alignment with the reported decline.
No routing-change event is present, and the data provide no direct evidence of a configuration change affecting call distribution.
Some queues experienced intermittent pressure, but the pattern was localized and variable rather than the exact, system-wide 26-point offset observed in the dashboard metric.
No platform event or broad call-processing disruption is recorded, and calls continued to be handled throughout the window.
Aggregate offered volume closely matched forecast, so forecast error was not material to the sustained dashboard alert.

stakeholder_summary: CC-012 was caused by a dashboard data-quality defect, not sustained contact-center underperformance. From 09:15 onward, reported service level was exactly 26 percentage points too low. Recalculated service exceeded the 80% target in all but two brief intervals; staffing and aggregate demand remained stable.
